condition_zh: 乙醛脱氢酶2缺乏症（酒精脸红反应）
condition_en: ALDH2 Deficiency (Alcohol Flush Reaction / Asian Flush)

east_asia.population: East Asian population (~36% ALDH2*2 allele carriers)

lab_tests: ALDH2 genotyping for rs671 (Glu504Lys / ALDH2*2 variant)
Ethanol patch test (skin erythema after topical ethanol)

thresholds.ALDH2_1_2_heterozygous: Partial ALDH2 activity (~6-10% of normal) — some flushing, elevated acetaldehyde
thresholds.ALDH2_2_2_homozygous: No ALDH2 activity — severe flushing, very high acetaldehyde levels, cannot tolerate alcohol

treatment.method: Complete alcohol abstinence or strict minimization
treatment.indication: All ALDH2-deficient individuals — the ONLY evidence-based recommendation

treatment.method: Upper endoscopy surveillance for esophageal cancer
treatment.indication: ALDH2-deficient individuals who drink alcohol AND smoke

risk_factors: Combined ALDH2 deficiency + alcohol consumption → 6-10x increased esophageal squamous cell carcinoma risk
Combined ALDH2 deficiency + alcohol + smoking → 50-100x increased esophageal cancer risk
complications: Acetaldehyde is a Group 1 carcinogen (IARC) — ALDH2 deficiency dramatically increases its accumulation
prevention: Alcohol abstinence in ALDH2-deficient individuals (strongest preventive measure)
Genetic screening for ALDH2 status before establishing drinking habits
Public health education about 'Asian flush' as a cancer risk signal, NOT a cosmetic issue

clinical_examples.description: A 35-year-old businessman from Fujian presents with concern about his facial flushing after drinking beer with clients. He drinks 2-3 bottles of beer 3-4 times weekly. He also smokes 10 cigarettes/day. He considers the flushing 'normal' and uses antihistamines to mask symptoms. His father died of esophageal cancer at age 58.
clinical_examples.key_findings: ALDH2 deficiency (confirmed ALDH2*1/*2 heterozygous) + regular alcohol + smoking + family history of esophageal cancer → extremely high risk for ESCC
clinical_examples.outcome: Counseled on the 50-100x elevated esophageal cancer risk. Strongly advised alcohol cessation and smoking cessation. Referred for upper endoscopy screening. ALDH2 deficiency explained as a genetic risk factor — antihistamines mask flushing but do NOT reduce acetaldehyde accumulation and cancer risk.

citations.title: ALDH2 Genotype, Alcohol Consumption, and the Risk of Esophageal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
The Alcohol Flushing Response: An Unrecognized Risk Factor for Esophageal Cancer from Alcohol Consumption
